title: sales-partnership-scratch-notes-tyler-cho
content:
Account: Helix Health / helixhealth.com
Why target: strong need for HIPAA-compliant private inference; recent funding (Series B Oct 2025) and hiring ML infra lead — good timing.
Key contacts (LinkedIn):
  - Priya Nair — Director of ML Platforms (hiring ML infra lead mentioned in post)
  - Daniel Ruiz — Head of Engineering (owner of vendor evals historically)
  - Lauren Cho — Chief Product Officer (interested in clinical summarization use cases)
Notes / signals:
  - Posted job for "Inference Platform Engineer" (req 4567) — indicates they'll be building infra but likely want vendor for speed.
  - Security/compliance = must-have (HIPAA, SOC2).
  - Current stack hints: AWS, Sagemaker noted in job/tech blog.
  - Customer quote on Crunchbase: "focus on fast reliable inference for clinical notes".

Top value props to emphasize (short):
  - Private deployment + KMS/HSM support for PHI (Redwood Private) — beats generic hosted APIs.
  - Predictable latency + autoscaling for peak inference loads (clinical spike patterns) — Dedicated offering.
  - Cost controls: batching, quantization + visibility in Console (token-level cost breakdown) — helps justify ROI vs building in-house.
  - Rollouts & regression protection: canary model rollouts + eval hooks to avoid degradation in clinical metrics.

Outbound drafts (email / short):
1) Short intro — initial cold outreach
Subject: Quick question on inference for clinical workflows
Hi Priya,
I saw Helix's job posting for an Inference Platform Engineer and thought it might be a good time to introduce Redwood. We help teams run large models with predictable latency and PHI-safe private deployments — lots of folks in healthcare use Redwood Private + Dedicated to avoid building infra from scratch.
Would you be open to a 20-min intro next week? I can share a short pilot plan tailored to clinical summarization workloads.
Best,
Tyler

2) Follow-up + value add (2 days later)
Subject: One-pager: private inference + HIPAA-friendly pilot
Priya —
Attaching a quick one-pager (link below) showing a 4-week pilot we ran with a similar health-tech customer: reduced per-call cost by ~40% and maintained <200ms p95 latency for summary endpoint. Happy to walk through the plan.
Link: CON-1234 (pilot-one-pager)

LinkedIn InMail (short)
Hi Priya, saw your post about expanding infra — would love to share a 15-min pilot concept for running clinical LLMs with PHI-safe private deployments. Quick availability next week?

Discovery questions to use if intro accepted:
  - What are your latency p95 targets for summarization / triage endpoints?
  - Typical request size (tokens) and QPS during peaks?
  - Is PHI in transit or stored? What KMS/HSM requirements do you have?
  - Current model(s) you're evaluating (open weights, vendor models)?
  - Owners for security sign-off / procurement timeline?

Objection handling / quick rebuttals:
  - "We can build this ourselves": + acknowledge — "you could, but typical build takes 6-9 months; Redwood gives a predictable SLA + ops tooling in weeks and can hand off runbook"; offer a TCO side-by-side for first 12 months.
  - "Cost concerns": share batching + quantization levers, highlight Console cost breakdown and 4-week pilot to measure real numbers. Offer credits for pilot.
  - "Security/compliance": point to Private offering, KMS/HSM integration, SOC2 compliance notes (we'll provide detailed security docs & support procurement).
  - "Vendor lock-in": emphasize model versioning + ability to deploy same runtime privately (we support self-hosted control plane options).

Competitive notes (quick):
  - Generic cloud AI vendors: lower setup but lack private deployment + audit features for PHI.
  - Specialty inference runtimes: strong performance but often require more build ops; our differentiator is integrated console + rollout tooling + cost controls.

Pilot idea (4-week, minimal scope):
  Week 0: kickoff + security questionnaire + simplest private deployment (VPC)
  Week 1: baseline measurement (latency/cost) using their model or Redwood curated open model
  Week 2: apply batching/quantization + runtime tuning
  Week 3: run acceptance tests + produce cost/latency report + handoff plan
Deliverables: pilot report, runbook for production, 30-day follow-up. Offer: discounted dedicated hours + 2-week free usage credits.

Internal TODOs / next steps (Tyler):
  - Pull contact email for Priya (LinkedIn / Clearbit) — due 2026-03-03
  - Draft pilot one-pager (link CON-1234) — 2 days
  - Align SRE/solutions on HIPAA checklist for private pilots — ping Samir
  - Prepare TCO template + similar customer case (ask Maya for past healthcare pilot deck)

Quick links / references:
  - CON-1234 (pilot-one-pager)
  - JIRA-7890 (legal: access requirements for PHI pilots)
  - Helix job posting: https://jobs.example.com/helix/inference-platform-engineer (save screenshot in thread)

Notes-to-self: keep outreach short, use case-first language (clinical summarization), offer clear safety/ops guarantees. If Priya is non-responsive, pivot to Daniel Ruiz (Head Eng) and call out procurement timeline and cost model directly.

End of note.
